summary: Siskiyou NF summit lookout: 1914 shake cabin, 1928 D-6 cab, 1955 10-ft L-4 tower; removed 1958; a Forest Service trail and 1984 plaque are on the summit today.

facts.status_note: Tower removed in 1958; a summit plaque and the trail remain, and no source describes lookout remains

staffing.status: lookout staffed through at least 1941 (120 days a year)

access.note: Mt. Bolivar Trail #1259 is open to hiking only, in the Wild Rogue Wilderness; 1.4 miles one way

visit.trail_note: 1.4 miles one way, hiking only; drive from Powers via County Road 90, Forest Road 33 and Forest Road 3348

events.note: Shake cabin, 12 feet square, completed by November 1914; corners anchored to bedrock with telephone wire
District Ranger R.I. Helm planned to train Guard Price on the map and sighting device
Small smoke seen June 18 while the fire finder was installed; by August the lookout had reported 22 fires (8 inside, 14 outside the forest)
1,600-gallon water tank erected for the lookout
Snow slide carried the water tank about 300 feet down the hillside
D-6 style house replaced the shake cabin; lumber cut in Grants Pass and packed about 20 miles on horseback; set on a 10-foot tower
Andrew Flynn, formerly a clerk at CCC district headquarters, received the lookout position near Powers
Station staffed 120 days; reporting station the Powers Ranger Station
Aircraft Warning Service station active March 10 to July 16; Roseburg Filter Center listed
New 10-foot L-4 tower (firetower.org and firelookout.com); the Oregon lookouts history dates the new house to 1957 after a July 30, 1955 report of bids being readied
Lookout building and tower removed; all three sources give 1958

corrections.why: The record names only the 1928 cab. The last structure on the summit was a 10-foot L-4 tower, which both firetower.org and firelookout.com date to 1955 and removal in 1958.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firetower.org and firelookout.com date the 10-foot L-4 tower to 1955; the Oregon lookouts history says a new lookout house was constructed in 1957, after a July 30, 1955 report of bids being readied. The story gives 1955 with the 1957 date noted.

notes_for_editor: The brief's design D-6 (height 3.0 m) matches the 1928 cab on a 10-foot tower; the final 1955 structure was a 10-foot L-4 tower, so the correction adds it rather than replacing the 1928 entry. The 1955 vs 1957 date for the final house is unresolved and the story says so. The FS trail page and a 1984 plaque are the only present-day features described; no source describes lookout remains. The Oregon lookouts page quotes 1914-1942 Siskiyou Bulletin and newspaper items; quotes were checked against that page. Confidence is high for the 1914, 1928 and 1958 dates, which agree across sources. Checked 2026-10-09: wording now matches the cited pages (bids were being readied, not requested; the 1934 appointment is a position received; the 1928 materials and the summit plaque are paraphrased); the steep-slope detail is backed by a December 1914 quote.
